verses.1: For the leader; with stringed instruments. A psalm of David.
verses.2: Answer when I call, my saving God. In my troubles, you cleared a way; show me favor; hear my prayer.
verses.3: How long will you people mock my honor, love what is worthless, chase after lies? Selah
verses.4: Know that the LORD works wonders for the faithful; the LORD hears when I call out.
verses.5: Tremble and do not sin; upon your beds ponder in silence.
verses.6: Offer fitting sacrifice and trust in the LORD.
verses.7: Many say, "May we see better times! LORD, show us the light of your face!" Selah
verses.8: But you have given my heart more joy than they have when grain and wine abound.
verses.9: In peace I shall both lie down and sleep, for you alone, LORD, make me secure.

notes.text: For the leader: many psalm headings contain this rubric. Its exact meaning is unknown but may signify that such psalms once stood together in a collection of "the choirmaster." Cf
Tremble: be moved deeply with religious awe. The Greek translation understood the emotion to be anger, and it is so cited in Eph 4:26.
